note: Item wording = level-1 data labels: the source workbook's column headers ARE the item text. data/dou2025_aesthetics.py assigns codes positionally (area_{i+1} over raw.columns[27:39]), so the positional step was re-run against the downloaded raw.xlsx: the 12 headers at those positions are the AReA block, and their per-column means/SDs over the 748 valid respondents reproduce the deposit's own SPSS descriptives on Sheet2 (re1-re5, r1-r4, rb1-rb3) to 4 dp and in order -- e.g. area_1 3.6832/0.88563 = re1, area_11 2.6578/1.24635 = rb2, area_12 3.1070/1.15785 = rb3; live per-item n is 748 for all 12 (irw_table_sets), matching. Instrument confirmed as the 12-item Chinese revision of the AReA (Peng & Chen, 2023), 1-5 Likert, per the paper's Measures section; not the 18-item Schlotz et al. (2021) original, and not the paper's other two scales (ANS 1-6, WCTS). Rights checked before transcribing: the source article and its figshare deposit are CC BY 4.0 (PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0331067), and the AReA's own distribution page (edvessel.com/area, OSF downloads) states no non-commercial clause, no fee and no redistribution bar -- nothing quotable fires the SKILL's rights rules. No instructions text is published in either the deposit or the paper, so instructions/section_prompt are blank. option_text is the paper's English endpoint gloss, not administered Chinese anchors (see notes).
public_note: The English item_text_translated for this table was produced by IRW, not by the study authors; and its response anchors are shipped as the paper's English gloss (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree) because the Chinese wording respondents actually saw for the scale points is not published in the deposit or the paper.
